title: Air-gapped install lab test plan — Signed offline bundles (v1)
body:
Doc purpose
Validate end-to-end installation of Redwood Private in a realistic air-gapped environment using signed offline bundles (images + charts/manifests + binaries + metadata), with verification enforced offline and fail-closed by default.

This plan is intended to be executed in the Private Deployments lab to gate Phase 2→Phase 3 (pilot readiness). It covers: (1) positive install path, (2) negative/tamper paths, (3) upgrade/rollback sanity, (4) logging/evidence collection.

Owners / roles
- Test coordinator: Fatima Noor (SE, air-gapped SME)
- Installer verification: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
- Networking/offline constraints: Victor Alvarez / Irene Choi
- Security sign-off on break-glass and evidence: Marcus Lin
- Support readiness and diagnostics checklist: Dev Patel

Scope (what we are testing)
In-scope
- Offline bundle verification: signature + manifest integrity + per-artifact digests (fail-closed)
- Offline install flow with no outbound network calls
- Usability of error messages and remediation steps
- Audit logging / evidence artifacts (installer logs, verification summary, provenance references)
- Media transfer and offline repository workflows (USB + offline registry option)

Out of scope (for this lab pass)
- Customer-managed signing keys (v1 non-goal)
- Complex enterprise integrations (SAML/SCIM, custom HSM on customer side) unless required for air-gapped basic install
- Performance benchmarking (throughput/latency) beyond a basic smoke test

Success criteria summary (acceptance gates)
Gate A — Offline verification correctness
- Installer verifies bundle signature fully offline.
- If signature invalid OR manifest modified OR any artifact digest mismatch → install must stop (non-zero exit) before unpack/apply.
- Verification includes downgrade protection behavior per spec (reject older bundle if policy configured / release channel constraints applied).

Gate B — Air-gap compliance
- During verify/install, no outbound network traffic is required.
- No calls to public endpoints for OCI pulls, chart fetches, key retrieval, time-stamping, CRL/OCSP, telemetry, etc.
- All dependencies provided via offline bundle and/or local on-prem infra (internal DNS/NTP allowed).

Gate C — Evidence + supportability
- Verification result produces a human-readable summary and a machine-readable record.
- Logs include enough fields to diagnose failures without leaking secrets.
- Break-glass override (if used) requires explicit acknowledgement and is clearly recorded.

Gate D — Reproducibility
- Bundle manifest is deterministic for the same input release (as defined in spec). (We’ll check for stable ordering + stable digests; we are not requiring byte-identical tarball packaging in this pass.)

Test environment overview
We simulate a regulated customer environment with two network zones:
- Connected zone (“build/transfer host”): can access Redwood artifact store + CI outputs. Used to download the offline bundle.
- Air-gapped zone (“offline install environment”): no internet. Receives artifacts only via removable media or an offline registry.

Network rules (must be enforced)
- Air-gapped zone:
  - No default route to internet.
  - DNS resolves only internal lab zones.
  - NTP is internal only (or time set manually for deterministic behavior tests).
  - Kubernetes nodes cannot pull from public registries.
  - If the installer attempts any outbound call, we should see it blocked in logs/pcap.

Hardware / software matrix (lab)
We’ll run the core test on two OS families to approximate customer variance.

Matrix table (target)
1) Transfer / staging host (connected)
- HW: Dell R740, 32 cores, 128GB RAM, 2TB SSD
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS
- Tools: curl/wget, sha256sum, gpg (optional for local checks), usbutils
- Purpose: download signed bundle + signatures; stage media; optionally run pre-flight verify

2) Air-gapped control host (offline)
- HW: Supermicro 1U, 16 cores, 64GB RAM, 1TB SSD
- OS A: RHEL 9.2 (primary)
- OS B: Ubuntu 22.04.4 (secondary run)
- Purpose: run redwood-private-installer verify + install; collect logs

3) Kubernetes cluster (offline)
- Topology: 3 control-plane/worker nodes (or 1 control-plane + 2 workers depending on lab capacity)
- K8s: v1.28.x (confirm exact patch per current Private support)
- Runtime: containerd 1.7.x
- CNI: Calico (default lab) or Cilium (optional)
- Ingress: NGINX (lab standard)
- Storage: local-path for smoke; optional: NFS provisioner for closer-to-customer behavior

4) Optional GPU node (offline) — if required by Redwood Private minimal serving deployment
- HW: 1x NVIDIA L40S or A10 (lab availability)
- Driver: aligned with Redwood Private support matrix
- Purpose: validate image pull + runtime on GPU node without internet

Software under test
- Redwood Private installer build: from release candidate branch for offline bundle verification (see linked PRs)
- Offline bundle version: v1 format (manifest schema version per Confluence spec)
- Signing cert/public key: pinned verification material included with installer or shipped in bundle (confirm final approach)

Inputs / artifacts needed
- Signed offline bundle (.tar.zst or equivalent) containing:
  - OCI images (as tar archives and/or OCI layout) required for Private deployment
  - Helm charts / manifests for control plane + serving components
  - Required binaries/tools packaged for offline use (if any)
  - Bundle manifest (JSON)
  - Detached signature + signing envelope files
  - Checksums (if separate)
  - SBOM/provenance references if implemented in v1
- Verification keys/certs:
  - Embedded in installer OR delivered via a secure, documented offline method
  - Known “test key” for negative tests (non-prod) to validate failure behavior

Outputs to collect (for evidence + troubleshooting)
For each run, collect the following into a single folder with timestamp:
- Installer logs (stdout/stderr capture)
- Verification summary output (human-readable)
- Machine-readable verification record (if present)
- Bundle manifest used
- Hashes of bundle files as transferred (sha256 of tarball + signature file)
- Network evidence (optional but recommended): tcpdump on offline host during verify/install to show no outbound connections
- Kubernetes events + pod status after install (kubectl get pods -A, describe failing pods)

Test cases

TC0 — Environment sanity checks (pre-run)
Goal: Ensure the air-gap is real and we won’t accidentally pass due to cached resources.
Steps:
1. On offline control host, confirm:
   - No default route to internet
   - /etc/resolv.conf points to internal DNS only
   - iptables / firewall denies outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 (except internal ranges)
2. Confirm container runtime has no pre-pulled Redwood images:
   - crictl images | grep redwood (should be empty or documented baseline)
3. Clear any local chart caches used by the installer (document path if applicable).
Expected:
- No internet route.
- No Redwood images cached.
- Baseline documented.

TC1 — Happy path (USB transfer, verify + install)
Goal: Validate the primary customer workflow: download bundle in connected zone, transfer via removable media, verify offline, then install.
Steps:
1. Connected zone:
   - Download bundle and signature artifacts from artifact storage.
   - Record sha256 of bundle + signature files.
2. Transfer:
   - Copy to encrypted USB drive (or lab-approved removable media).
   - Safely eject.
3. Offline zone:
   - Copy artifacts from USB to /var/tmp/redwood-offline/<release>/
   - Run installer verification command:
     - redwood-private-installer verify --bundle <path>
   - Confirm verification passes.
   - Run install command using the bundle:
     - redwood-private-installer install --bundle <path> [other required flags]
4. Post-install smoke:
   - Confirm all required namespaces/pods are Running.
   - Run a basic health check endpoint (internal) or Redwood Console readiness check if available.
Expected:
- verify returns 0; outputs signature subject/key id and bundle version/release id.
- install proceeds only after verify success.
- cluster comes up without pulling anything from internet.
Artifacts:
- Save logs + verification record.

TC2 — Happy path (offline registry path)
Goal: Validate option where bundle content is loaded into an on-prem registry (common for customers).
Steps:
1. Offline zone: stand up local registry (Harbor or registry:2) reachable by cluster nodes.
2. Load bundle images into local registry using provided tooling.
3. Install referencing local registry endpoints.
Expected:
- No external pulls.
- Image references rewritten correctly.
- Installer still verifies the bundle signature before load/apply.

TC3 — Tamper test: modify manifest after signing
Goal: Ensure signature verification fails on any manifest modification.
Steps:
1. Copy a valid bundle to a test location.
2. Edit a single character in the manifest JSON (e.g., whitespace change if signature covers the canonical form; if canonicalization exists, change a field value).
3. Run verify.
Expected:
- verify fails with clear message (signature mismatch / manifest integrity failure).
- install is blocked.

TC4 — Tamper test: corrupt an included artifact
Goal: Ensure digest checking catches corruption introduced during transfer.
Steps:
1. Copy bundle.
2. Flip a byte in one of the packaged OCI layer blobs or chart tgz (use dd).
3. Run verify.
Expected:
- verify fails citing which artifact digest mismatched.
- install blocked.
Notes:
- This also simulates real-world media errors.

TC5 — Wrong key / untrusted signer
Goal: Ensure only authorized signing keys are accepted.
Steps:
1. Use a bundle signed with a non-trusted test key (or modify verification trust store to exclude expected key).
2. Run verify.
Expected:
- verify fails with message indicating signer not trusted / key id not allowed.

TC6 — Break-glass override flow (explicit acknowledgement)
Goal: Validate emergency override requires explicit acknowledgement and leaves audit trail.
Precondition:
- Use a tampered bundle (from TC3/TC4) so verify fails.
Steps:
1. Attempt install without override → should fail.
2. Attempt install with break-glass override flag.
3. Confirm the CLI forces explicit acknowledgement text entry or confirm prompt (per implementation).
Expected:
- Without override: blocked.
- With override: proceeds only after explicit acknowledgement.
- Logs clearly indicate override used, reason captured if supported, and includes operator identity fields if available.
Security note:
- We do NOT treat successful install under break-glass as a “pass”; we treat it as a pass only if the friction + logging meets the policy.

TC7 — Downgrade / replay protection behavior
Goal: Ensure policy prevents accidental/unauthorized rollback when configured.
Steps (depending on implemented mechanism):
1. Install a newer release bundle.
2. Attempt to verify+install an older bundle.
Expected:
- If policy forbids downgrades: installer rejects with clear error.
- If policy allows downgrades: requires explicit flag or additional acknowledgement (confirm desired behavior with spec).

TC8 — Time validity edge case (offline clock)
Goal: Ensure verification doesn’t require OCSP/CRL and handles time reasonably offline.
Steps:
1. Set offline host clock to a date outside certificate validity range (if cert validity is used).
2. Run verify.
Expected:
- Behavior matches spec:
  - Either fails with clear “certificate not valid at this time” without attempting network,
  - or uses a trust model that doesn’t require time validation (only if explicitly designed that way).
Notes:
- This is important for truly isolated environments with poor time sync.

TC9 — Partial transfer / missing signature file
Goal: Ensure missing files fail closed with actionable error.
Steps:
1. Remove detached signature file.
2. Run verify.
Expected:
- verify fails with “signature file missing” (or equivalent).
- install blocked.

TC10 — Installer logging completeness
Goal: Ensure logs contain required fields for support and compliance.
Steps:
1. Run TC1 (happy path) and TC4 (digest mismatch).
2. Review logs for:
   - bundle version / release id
   - manifest schema version
   - signer key id / cert subject
   - verification outcome + reason code
   - list of failing artifacts (for mismatch cases) without dumping sensitive content
Expected:
- Fields present and consistent.
- No secret material printed.

Execution plan / schedule
- Day 1: TC0 + TC1 on RHEL offline host; capture evidence and any installer UX gaps.
- Day 2: TC3/TC4/TC5 negative cases; iterate on error strings and logging if needed.
- Day 3: TC2 (offline registry) + TC6 break-glass; security review of override evidence.
- Day 4 (optional): Repeat TC1 on Ubuntu offline host; run TC7/TC8.

Runbook-style notes (operator tips)
- Prefer copying bundle to local disk before verifying to reduce USB performance variability.
- Always record sha256 before and after transfer. If sha differs pre-verify, treat as media issue and still run TC4-style analysis.
- If the installer shells out to tooling (e.g., tar/zstd/oci loaders), capture versions for reproducibility.

Failure triage checklist
When a test fails, capture:
- exact command invoked
- full stdout/stderr
- bundle file list (ls -lah)
- sha256 of bundle + signature files
- verification error code (if provided)
- any “expected vs got” digests printed
- tcpdump snippet if there’s any suspicion of blocked network calls

Open questions (to resolve before final sign-off)
1. What is the authoritative offline trust root: embedded in installer vs shipped alongside bundle vs customer-configurable trust store?
2. What is the canonicalization strategy for the manifest before signing (if any)? This affects TC3 expectations (whitespace vs field change).
3. Downgrade policy: is it enforced by default, optional, or tied to a release channel?
4. Time validity enforcement: do we require accurate time to verify? If yes, what’s the recommended offline NTP story?

Sign-off
This test plan is considered complete when:
- All “Gate A/B/C” tests pass in at least one OS path (RHEL), and
- Negative tests demonstrate fail-closed behavior, and
- Security (Marcus Lin) approves break-glass logging + acknowledgement UX, and
- Support (Dev Patel) confirms diagnostics are sufficient for customer escalation.

Change log
- 2025-01-17: Initial draft created (Fatima)
- 2025-01-28: Added negative/tamper tests + break-glass steps (Fatima/Ethan)
- 2025-02-06: Added offline registry path + logging completeness checks (Fatima/Dev)
